title: Fix the average response size
prompt: This job reports the average response size per HTTP method, but the numbers don't match a hand count, and it crashes when a method has a single request. Fix `solve(api_requests)` so `avg_bytes` is the true average of `bytes_sent` per `method`.
rules: One row per `method` that has at least one request with a `bytes_sent`. Requests with a missing `bytes_sent` are left out.
`avg_bytes` is the sum of the values divided by how many there are, not rounded.
Return `method` (text) and `avg_bytes` (`double`), in that order. Keep repeated requests.
hints: Work the starter's function by hand on three values, 10, 20 and 60. Does it give 30?
`reduceByKey` combines values two at a time in any order, so averaging pairs isn't the average of all of them.
Carry `(sum, count)`, add both parts, and divide once at the end with `mapValues`. That also makes every result a float.
explanation: `(a + b) / 2` averages two values at a time, so with three or more values the answer depends on the order they were combined in: 10, 20 and 60 give 37.5, 27.5 or 25, never 30. A method with one request is never combined at all, so its value stays a Python `int`, which a `double` column refuses. Carry `(bytes_sent, 1)`, add both parts in `reduceByKey`, and finish with `mapValues(lambda s: s[0] / s[1])`; `/` always gives a float.
